title: Surging Earnings Estimates Signal Upside for Chime Financial, Inc. (CHYM) Stock
author: Zacks.Com
description: Chime Financial, Inc. (CHYM) has received a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating due to strong upward earnings estimate revisions. The company is expected to earn $0.17 per share for the current quarter (up 241.7% year-over-year) and $0.47 for the full year (up 111.0%). Over the past 30 days, five analyst estimates have been raised with no negative revisions, pushing consensus estimates higher. The stock has gained 6.8% over the past four weeks, with analysts suggesting further upside potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong upward earnings estimate revisions with 5 positive revisions and zero negative revisions over the past month. Current quarter EPS expected to grow 241.7% year-over-year and full-year EPS expected to grow 111.0%. Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating indicates analyst confidence in future performance. Stock has already gained 6.8% in four weeks with potential for further upside.

title: Why Chime Financial, Inc. (CHYM) is a Top Momentum Stock for the Long-Term
author: Zacks.Com
description: Chime Financial, Inc. (CHYM), a San Francisco-based fintech company that went public in June 2025, has been identified as a top momentum stock. The company holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating with a VGM Score of B and Momentum Style Score of B. Six analysts revised earnings estimates upward in the last 60 days, with the consensus estimate increasing to $0.47 per share for fiscal 2026. Shares are up 6.8% over the past four weeks, and the company boasts an average earnings surprise of +310%.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: CHYM receives a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating with strong momentum indicators including a B Momentum Style Score, 6.8% share price increase over four weeks, six upward earnings estimate revisions in 60 days, and an exceptional +310% average earnings surprise, indicating strong analyst confidence and positive market performance.

title: Chime Financial, Inc. (CHYM) Surpasses Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
author: Zacks.Com
description: Chime Financial reported Q3 2026 earnings of $0.15 per share, beating consensus estimates of $0.09 by 66.67%, and revenues of $718 million, exceeding estimates by 1.82%. The company has beaten consensus estimates for four consecutive quarters. With a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating, the stock is expected to outperform the market in the near term, though the Financial - Miscellaneous Services industry ranks in the bottom 37% of Zacks industries.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company significantly beat both EPS estimates (+66.67%) and revenue estimates (+1.82%), has beaten consensus estimates four consecutive quarters, received a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) rating, and outperformed S&P 500 year-to-date (+12% vs +10.6%). However, sentiment is tempered by the weak industry outlook.

Company has not yet reported Q3 results. Expected to post earnings of $0.53 per share (+17.8% YoY) with revenues of $976.77 million (+14.2% YoY), but consensus EPS estimate was revised 1.8% lower over the last 30 days, indicating slightly weakening expectations.

title: MSTR Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Bitcoin Gains Despite Revenue Miss
author: Na
description: Strategy Inc. (MSTR) reported Q3 2026 EPS of $44.75, significantly beating the consensus estimate of $21.50, driven primarily by a $20.91 billion gain on its digital assets. The company's bitcoin holdings reached 848,517 BTC as of October 25, 2026, with USD assets climbing to $5.07 billion. However, total revenues declined 2.5% year-over-year to $125.43 million, missing estimates, though subscription services revenues grew 49.2%. The company raised $21.23 billion year-to-date through stock offerings.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong EPS beat of 431.5% year-over-year growth and significant gains on bitcoin holdings demonstrate robust profitability. Growing subscription revenues (+49.2%) and expanding bitcoin holdings (+26% YTD) indicate positive momentum. However, sentiment is tempered by declining total revenues and traditional product sales, suggesting reliance on volatile digital asset valuations rather than core business growth.
